{{Vanilla|Anvil}}
{{Infobox auto}}
An '''anvil''' is a block used to repair equipment, rename items and apply enchanted books. In [[Matcha Flavoured]] it is the only way to apply [[blessing]]s and other [[enchanting|enchantments]], and the pack changes how experience and repair costs work with it so that repairs never become too expensive.

== Obtaining ==
=== Crafting ===
{{Recipes}}
The pack adds a cheaper recipe that uses three [[Steel Alloy]] in place of the three blocks of iron.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/anvil.json}}</ref> The vanilla recipe with blocks of iron is still in the game, although the {{Version|1.03}} release notes say it was removed; see [[#Notes|Notes]].

== Usage ==
=== Applying enchantments ===
Blessings, [[Ofuda]] and found books are combined with equipment in an anvil, as in vanilla. The pack lowers the anvil cost multiplier of every vanilla enchantment to 1 and of most of its own enchantments to 0, so combining books costs few levels.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/enchantment/unbreaking.json}}</ref>

=== Repairing ===
{{Main|Repairing}}
Equipment is repaired in the anvil with its base material. The "Repair & Reuse" advancement describes this: "Anvils made from Steel can repair Any Equipment with its corresponding Base-Metal Ingot forever". Repairing in the crafting grid is disabled.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.1-alpha|quote=Repairing Equipment in the crafting menu is now disabled}}</ref>

=== Experience ===
Whenever a player uses an anvil (a normal, chipped or damaged one), the pack sets their experience level to 10,000, so anvil work never fails for lack of levels.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/require_xp.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/block/grants_temp_levels.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/xp_handling/give_levels.mcfunction}}</ref> Players also get 10,000 levels when they first join a world, and again the first time they join after the pack is updated.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/update_this_player.mcfunction}}</ref> The levels are never taken away. The high number is chosen so that the level-up sound plays rarely. The player doesn't see their experience: the resource pack draws the experience bar without its fill, and its language files replace the level number and the anvil's "Enchantment Cost" line with empty text.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/textures/gui/sprites/hud/experience_bar_progress.png}}</ref><ref name="lang">{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref> This works only in the languages whose file in the resource pack blanks these texts: in others, such as Finnish or Afrikaans, the game's own translation wins and the number shows.<ref name="lang" />

In {{Version|1.12.7-beta}} and {{Version|1.12.8-beta}} a text shader hid the level number instead. It made interface text invisible when it was drawn in the level number's green or its black outline color; in 1.12.7-beta it had no position check, so all black interface text vanished, and signs being edited and books being read appeared blank. 1.12.8-beta limited it to the bottom quarter of the screen.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/shaders/core/text.vsh|at=34a04e6571d9ee6f0cc1d8d50cdfa85980720156}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/shaders/core/text.vsh|at=58e88dcec369fe3293fb25a15214249d116a100e}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.8-beta|quote=Signs and Books no longer appear blank}}</ref> The release notes explain the reason: data packs cannot remove the experience requirement from anvil repairs.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.6-alpha|quote=XP is not shown unless you interact with an anvil, since I can't remove XP requirements for anvil repairing}}</ref>

Up to 1.12.6-alpha, the pack instead set every player's level and points to 0 each tick. After a player opened an anvil, the next change to their inventory gave them 100 levels and exempted them from the reset until a 31-second timer, shared by all players and restarted by any player's inventory change, ran out.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/anvil_xp/remove_xp.mcfunction|at=fe225857ed8af507b7f5755f4d41678f6862b1bd}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/anvil_xp/check_anvil_interaction.mcfunction|at=fe225857ed8af507b7f5755f4d41678f6862b1bd}}</ref>

=== Repair cost ===
Every time the player's inventory changes, the prior-work penalty (the <code>repair_cost</code> component) of every item in the main inventory and hotbar is reset to 0. The penalty therefore never builds up, and items can be repaired and re-enchanted any number of times.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/endless_repairs/function/reset_breakable_repair_cost.mcfunction}}</ref> This part of the pack, in the <code>endless_repairs</code> namespace, is based on MiziraGamez's "Repair Cost Remover" data pack.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/endless_repairs/README.txt}}</ref> Items in the armor slots and offhand are not reset until they are moved into the inventory. Since {{Version|1.12.8-beta}} only items whose repair cost isn't already 0 are rewritten. Before, every item in those slots was rewritten on each inventory change, which deleted the contents of Traveler's Backpacks and other modded backpacks.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/endless_repairs/function/reset_breakable_repair_cost.mcfunction|at=34a04e6571d9ee6f0cc1d8d50cdfa85980720156}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.8-beta|quote=Traveler’s Backpacks (and other backpack mods) now do not delete its contents in Matcha}}</ref>

== Appearance ==
The pack retextures the anvil with a brick-red color. The developer confirmed this is intended, so that anvils can be used in brick builds.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12|quote=The Anvil texture thing isn't a bug, I did it so I could build with brick-coloured anvils}}</ref>

{{History|
{{History line|0.6-alpha|Experience is hidden unless the player interacts with an anvil.}}
{{History line|1.03|Added an error sprite for anvil smithing. The release notes say the anvil can no longer be crafted from blocks of iron.}}
{{History line|1.10|Anvils and anvil experience work in multiplayer. The experience timer increased from 15 to 30 seconds, and the levels given from 50 to 100.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.10|quote=Increased anvil xp timer from 15s to 30, and increased levels from 50 to 100}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.7-beta|Experience is no longer removed after using an anvil. Using an anvil sets the player's level to 10,000 instead of giving 100 levels for 30 seconds, and the resource pack hides the level number.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/xp_handling/give_levels.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.7-beta|quote=XP is no longer removed, since HapppySpud made a shader to block the XP number}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.8-beta|date=October 23, 2026|The shader that hides the level number now only hides text near the bottom of the screen, so the text of signs and books shows again.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.8-beta|quote=Signs and Books no longer appear blank}}</ref>
The repair cost reset no longer rewrites items whose repair cost is already 0, so modded backpacks keep their contents.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/endless_repairs/function/reset_breakable_repair_cost.mcfunction}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.9|The text shader is removed. }}

== Notes ==
* The vanilla anvil recipe (three blocks of iron and four iron ingots) is not blocked in the pack's <code>pack.mcmeta</code> filter, so it is still craftable despite the {{Version|1.03}} release notes.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.03|quote=Anvil can no longer be crafted from iron blocks (I dont want players spending too many resources on stuff if they don't have to)}}</ref>
